title: Divers found a 2,000-year-old computer in a shipwreck. #shorts

scenes.label: ANTIKYTHERA, GREECE
lines: In 1900, Greek sponge divers found a shipwreck more than two thousand years old.
Among what they brought up was a lump of corroded bronze.
It went to the National Archaeological Museum in Athens.

scenes.label: 17 MAY 1902
lines: In 1902, an archaeologist noticed something inside it.

scenes.label: 82 FRAGMENTS
lines: Today it survives in eighty-two fragments.
X-ray scans later revealed about thirty surviving bronze gears.
It predicted eclipses, the phases of the Moon, the planets, even the dates of the Olympic Games.

scenes.label: THE TWIST
lines: Nothing this complex appears again for more than a thousand years, not until the fourteenth century.
So who built it, and how was that knowledge lost?
Follow for one mystery every day.

youtube.title: Divers found a 2,000-year-old computer in a shipwreck. #shorts
youtube.description:
In 1900, Greek sponge divers found an ancient shipwreck off Antikythera. Among the finds was a corroded bronze lump. In 1902 archaeologist Valerios Stais noticed a gear wheel inside it. Today it survives as 82 fragments with about 30 bronze gears, and scans show it predicted eclipses, Moon phases, planetary positions and the Olympic Games cycle. Nothing this complex is known again until the 14th century.
